scope: Ayodhya Kanda Sargas 66–95, 90 linked verse-adjudication records

source_policy_evidence.finding: Publisher describes restrictions on copying volunteer-prepared content for promotion of a separate website and directs requesters to contact the publisher for intended use; personal study and research are distinguished from copying/reposting.
Site states volunteer-prepared files are intended for personal study/research and must not be copied or reposted for website promotion or commercial use without permission.

A separate Ramayana e-text index describes a Devanagari encoding originating from a published critical-edition encoding and separately links a Southern Recension and translations; this does not establish that RamaVerse's cited sarga witnesses use the same edition or may be redistributed.

risk_assessment.finding: No documented licence or explicit permission for RamaVerse to redistribute the cited digitised source transcription or third-party translated text.
risk_assessment.scope_limit: Publisher policy is not a determination of copyright subsistence in underlying ancient verses, and particular archived/mirrored pages may have additional terms. Verify individual provenance and permissions before copying any text.
risk_assessment.editorial_reference_and_linking: Evidence citations and independently written short review notes may be retained only subject to applicable legal/contractual assessment; do not treat a link as a reuse licence.

mandatory_release_conditions: Identify the actual edition/recension and source chain for each online witness; avoid equating the separate Baroda critical edition and Southern Recension.
Obtain explicit documented permission for any proposed reuse of Sanskrit Documents' prepared files or use a separately verified licensed/public-domain edition after provenance review.
Independently author and approve English and Tamil translations; do not reproduce third-party translations without rights.
Bind source identifiers, verse numbering, licences, publisher permissions and reviewer sign-offs in the versioned registry under its controlled workflow.
Keep all 90 noncanonical records on HOLD; do not publish, promote, merge or deploy as a result of this report.
limitations: Web policy observed 2026-11-12; no direct publisher correspondence or contract was reviewed.
Further source-specific licensing and legal interpretation may alter the risk assessment.
No source text, translation, digital edition or images are copied into this report.

witness_inventory.method: Read-only extraction of witness_url and publication_decision from all 90 review queue entries; hostnames treated literally (www and bare domain retained separately)
witness_inventory.publisher_scope: Every entry links to the Sanskrit Documents domain (including www alias); this is one website-level source-policy review cluster, not proof of one identical edition, license or file producer.
witness_inventory.limitations: HTTP links are cited editorial witnesses only; no bulk reuse authorization, edition binding or original text comparison is established by this host inventory.

observations.observation: The Valmiki subsection identifies itself as a mirror of www.valmikiramayan.net and describes experimental UTF-8 transposition of previously encoded verse files.
observations.inference_limit: Mirror documentation does not identify a single authoritative recension for every witness, establish licence grants, or resolve who holds rights in individual translations.

observations.observation: The separate e-text index attributes the valmikiramayan.net site to translators K. M. K. Murthy and Desiraju Hanumanta Rao; it separately describes the Baroda Critical Edition encoding and Southern Recension translation sources.
observations.inference_limit: Do not transfer the Baroda Critical Edition attribution to the 30 mirrored Ayodhya witness pages; do not infer the copyright status of translations from underlying ancient text.

observations.observation: Sample mirrored Sarga 66 page identifies chapter and verse locators and notes UTF-8 conversion in November 2009; it includes English glosses and translation alongside transliterated verses.
observations.inference_limit: A date of encoding or URL format does not establish legal reuse rights or independent edition authenticity.

observations.observation: Sample mirrored Sarga 69 page likewise includes Sanskrit transliteration, word glosses and English translation; its witness must not be treated as bare ancient text.
observations.inference_limit: This is sampled page inspection, not independent verification of all 30 pages.

sampled_passage_concordance_69_84_85.method: Direct side-by-side comparison of original-site ITRANS transliterated Sanskrit and GRETIL diacritic Sanskrit; selected verse openings, verse contents and narrative context were compared without copying complete text into this evidence file.

concordance.short_description: Bharata's ominous dream on the night messengers entered the city
Bharata is not cheered by his friends' entertainment
Dream narration continues; no explicit universal moral rule
Guha tells his people to defend Rama's interests by the Ganga
Sumantra describes Guha as Rama's friend
Bharata acknowledges Guha's offer of hospitality
Guha offers guides and his own accompaniment
Guha praises Bharata's willingness to relinquish the kingdom

sampled_passage_concordance_69_84_85.verse_number_warning: Original-site Ayodhya 84.3–84.5 and Southern 78.3–78.4 differ in verse segmentation/text. Therefore original 84.6 aligns with Southern 78.5, and original 84.12 with Southern 78.11. A constant chapter offset or copied verse index is UNSAFE.
limitations: Nine sample correspondences do not establish full chapter equivalence or shared textual recension.
Even aligned passages can have orthographic, lexical, sandhi and interpretive differences; all 90 records remain separately unreviewed by independent editors.
No permissions for reproducing GRETIL or valmikiramayan.net original digital texts, English translations or Tamil translations have been established.
The source registry must not be rewritten and no canonical record may be promoted on this evidence alone.

segmentation_exception.description: The original-site chapter uses an added/modified opening to the Bharata-identification passage and segments the following warning across three numbered verses; GRETIL compresses or differs in wording over two verses. Numeric offset conversion across this span is not valid.
segmentation_exception.next_review: Human philological check required for variants, omissions, additions and any manuscript/recension attribution; do not invent exact sub-verse correspondence.

sarga84_chapter_segmentation_audit.scope_limit: 15 straightforward passage-level verse alignments; three source verses map to a two-verse comparison span with textual differences. Neither chapter is declared an authoritative canonical replacement.
